title: You can hold the oil…
paragraphs:
You can hold the oil…
and still miss the Fire.

You can wave the handkerchief…
and never touch the Healer.

You can cling to symbols…
and slowly replace the Savior.
Pause.
Because this is where many hearts drift without noticing.

In Scripture, oil, cloths, even shadows were used by God—yes.
In Acts of the Apostles 19:11–12, handkerchiefs from Paul the Apostle carried healing.
But the power was never in the fabric.
It was always God.
And that’s the line we must not cross.

Because the human heart is subtle.
It takes what God uses…
and turns it into what it trusts.
That’s how a symbol becomes a substitute.

That’s how faith shifts—from the Living God…
to lifeless things.
But here’s what we miss…

God sometimes uses physical things as signs,
but He never asks you to trust the sign.
He asks you to trust Him.

The moment your confidence is in the oil,
instead of the One who anoints—
that’s not faith anymore.
That’s dependency on an object.

And Scripture is clear:
“Cursed is the one who trusts in man… or flesh…” (Book of Jeremiah 17:5)

Anything created can quietly become an idol—
even something that once pointed you to God.
Even something “spiritual.”
Even something used in church.
Let that sink in.
So what is real faith?

Not what you hold in your hand…
but Who holds your soul.

Not the oil on your head…
but the Spirit in your heart.

Not the cloth you carry…
but the cross you cling to.

Because salvation, healing, power—
they don’t come from elements.
They come from Jesus alone.
And here’s the grace…

If your heart drifted into trusting objects, rituals, or “spiritual tokens”—
you’re not condemned.
You’re being called back.
Back to simple, raw, unshaken faith.
Back to Christ.

No middleman.
No substitute.
No object needed.
Just Him.
So check your heart today:

Are you trusting the symbol…
or the Savior?
